merger_description:
BMD Fleet Pty Ltd (**BMD Fleet**), an existing shareholder in East Coast Commercial Vehicles, proposes to acquire the remaining shares of East Coast Commercial Vehicles held by BBMG Investments Pty Ltd (**BBMG**) and CRANEFM Investments Pty Ltd (**Crane**) (the **Acquisition**). Following the Acquisition, BMD Fleet will hold 100% of the shares in East Coast Commercial Vehicles.

East Coast Commercial Vehicles is the trading name of East Coast Commercial Vehicle Disposals Pty Ltd (**ECCVD**) and East Coast Commercial Vehicles (Gold Coast) Pty Ltd (**ECCGC**), which supply new and used commercial vehicles and certain related services (such as vehicle servicing and finance) from two motor vehicle dealerships located at 1169-1175 Beaudesert Road, Acacia Ridge, Queensland and 277 Scottsdale Drive, Robina, Queensland respectively.

BMD Fleet is an Australian company within the broader BMD Group, whose principal activities are in civil construction and infrastructure. BMD Fleet manages the vehicle fleet operated across the BMD Group.

BMD Constructions Pty Limited, a related entity to BMD Fleet within the BMD Group, holds a motor vehicle dealership licence and operates a small used vehicle dealership, Better Motor Deals, from its premises located at 7 Bingera Dr, Port of Brisbane QLD 4178. Better Motor Deals supplies the BMD Group's end-of-life (3–4-year-old) sports utility vehicles (**SUV**s) and light commercial vehicles (**LCV**s).

BBMG is a member of the Bartons Automotive Group, a Brisbane based automotive dealership group engaged in the retail sale and servicing of new and used vehicles (and ancillary services) in Brisbane's eastern suburbs of Wynnum and Capalaba. Crane holds a minority ownership interest in ECCVD and ECCGC.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of used
commercial vehicles (particularly SUVs and LCVs) in the
Gold Coast to Brisbane region of Queensland is low and the
increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition
would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of used commercial vehicles
(including SUVs and LCVs) to customers in the Gold Coast
to Brisbane region of Queensland, as well as south-east
Queensland more broadly
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
